turn.context: The approved shape: one big change, four small ones, two owners, then the ask. The decoupling is the hospital’s own answer from Diagnosis.

text: Process changes next. One big change, four small ones, and two owners.
bullets: The big one: admissions and discharges stop running one after the other. Two teams, or the two windows run together.
Four smaller changes hold it up. Each one costs a change in order, not money.
The bed plan is only as good as the discharge times it is built on. So both sides need an owner, and neither reports to the other.
chat.pointer: Switch between the day now and the day as it would run. Then pick a change or an owner.

question.text: Do you have someone on this job full time?
options: Yes, someone does it full time
We would look at creating the role
Tell me the reasoning in more detail

blocks.title: Run the two jobs together
blocks.deck: Today one team discharges, then admits. The change is to run both at once, against beds that will be free.

switch.cap_now: One team. Discharges first, then admissions. Patients reach a bed between 4:30 and 8 PM.
switch.cap_with: Both jobs run together, against beds that will be free. The goal is a bed by about noon.

blocks.caption: Your own times: patients arrive at about 1 PM and reach a bed between 4:30 and 8 PM. The noon time is a goal.

items.title: Give beds forward
items.text: Give a bed against when it will be free, not once it is ready.

items.title: A date a day ahead
items.text: The system shows the doctor a predicted date to check.

items.title: OPD advice first
items.text: Every planned admission starts from the advice in OPD.

items.title: One billing report
items.text: Bill close and bill open, read against the same bed.

sheets.title: Give beds forward
sheets.text: Today a bed is given only once it is confirmed ready. Give it against when it will be free instead. The same people and beds then make a different day.

lines.label: Costs
lines.value: Nothing but the order work is done in

sheets.entry: When does your desk give a bed today?

sheets.title: A date a day ahead
sheets.text: The doctor is shown a predicted discharge date to confirm or correct. That is a check, not a guess. It makes the evening plan possible.
sheets.entry: How early do your doctors say who goes home?

sheets.title: OPD advice first
sheets.text: Every planned admission starts from the doctor’s advice in OPD, with the date and the procedure. The mapping works from that.

lines.label: Needs
lines.value: The prescription, read as it is written

sheets.entry: Where does a planned admission start at your hospital?

sheets.title: One billing report
sheets.text: Both times already exist in billing. What does not exist is the join against the bed. That turns dead bed time into a number you can track.

blocks.label: Two owners
blocks.link: Peers. Neither reports to the other.
blocks.line: Give only one side an owner, and the side without one sets the pace.

owners.title: Bed Manager
owners.line: Holds tomorrow’s plan. Decides which patient goes to which bed, and when to call each one.

owners.title: Discharge Manager
owners.line: Owns every discharge, from the doctor’s word to the empty bed.

sheets.title: Bed Manager
sheets.text: Holds the plan, decides which patient goes to which bed, and sorts out late beds. On a busy day the patient at the desk wins, so a desk role cannot hold tomorrow’s plan.
sheets.entry: Does anyone hold the bed plan today?

sheets.title: Discharge Manager
sheets.text: Owns every discharge as one chain. Without this owner the Bed Manager spends the day chasing other people’s work.

lines.label: Needed above
lines.value: 80% of beds full or 40 patients a day

sheets.entry: Who chases a slow discharge today?

blocks.label: Discharge Manager
blocks.sub: Needed above 80% of beds full or 40 patients a day. You are at 89% and about 41. The 41 is worked out from your figures.
